claims.notes: Split from the volume statistics: when production ended is a separate, far better-evidenced fact than how many were made. This is the exact category of claim the audit used as its own worked example -- a historical fact ('production ended in 1988') classified timeless_or_historical_fact regardless of the modern publication date of the sources reporting it.

claims.normalized_claim: Cadillac marketed the Cimarron as a new kind of Cadillac aimed at a new kind of buyer, rather than as a smaller version of its existing cars.

sources.evidence_note: Cover reads in full: 'A NEW KIND OF CADILLAC FOR A NEW KIND OF CADILLAC OWNER.' Interior copy repeats 'An efficient new kind of Cadillac for a new kind of Cadillac owner' and 'a different kind of luxury car'.

forbidden_or_unsupported_inference: Inferring from this that Cadillac's buyer base was in fact aging or that the company was in fact losing younger buyers -- the brochure evidences the PITCH, not the market conditions behind it (see x02)
claims.notes: This claim exists to give the outline's 'why did Cadillac do this' beat something genuinely evidenced to stand on, replacing the unsourced aging-buyer-base assertion the audit flagged. A marketing pitch is an expressed, dated act -- perspective contemporary, not a historical data point -- which is why it's classified differently from the spec claims (e01-e04) even though they share a source.

Nothing about it is surprising or contradicted, so it stays medium and airable rather than blocked, but a second, independent source (a period comparison test that actually cross-shopped options) would be worth finding before this episode locks its script -- flagged in producer_outline.json's open_questions.

claims.normalized_claim: Cadillac pursued the Cimarron because its existing buyer base was aging and it was losing younger buyers to European compact sport sedans.
claims.safe_wording: Do not assert Cadillac's demographic motive as fact. What IS evidenced is how Cadillac PITCHED the car -- use c01 ('a new kind of Cadillac for a new kind of Cadillac owner') and c02 (the named rivals), which show the intent through the marketing without asserting the underlying market data.
forbidden_or_unsupported_inference: Presenting aging demographics, CAFE pressure, or lost younger buyers as documented causes of the Cimarron program
claims.notes: Causal claims about why a company made a decision are explicitly in the stronger-corroboration bucket, and this one has zero sources -- not a proportionality judgment call, just missing. Rather than delete the idea silently, it is recorded here as an explicitly unsourced, unresolved claim, so the gap is visible and a later research pass can close it. The outline beat has been rewritten to stand on c01/c02 instead.
